subject: Discovery Recap: Finly — p95 latency & concurrency requirements
messages:

Subject: Discovery Recap: Finly — p95 latency & concurrency requirements

Hi Jordan / Asha —

Thanks again for the chat today — really helpful to get visibility into the latency and throughput issues you're seeing in the payments UI and the agent assistant. Summary below, calling out pain, success criteria, and next steps so we're all aligned.

Quick summary of pain points (what you told us):
- Front-line agent assistant streaming responses degrade at p95: users see stalls and token bursts that break the streaming UX.
- Backend queued requests during peak payroll processing windows cause request spikes and long tail latency.
- Current provider-side throttles create retry storms and increased cost, and your on-call team spends time triaging.

Current stack (as we heard it):
- Customer-facing microservices in GCP (us-west1) calling a mixture of managed LLM endpoints + an in-house rule engine.
- Typical request: ~120 tokens prompt + streamed completion ~200 tokens.
- Peak concurrency target: target sustained 300 concurrent streams with bursts to ~1,000 for short windows.

Concrete success criteria (Finly engineering):
- P95 end-to-end token latency for short completions (<= 350 ms) for first bytes on streaming endpoints.
- Per-token streaming latency for subsequent tokens <= 200 ms to preserve perceived smoothness.
- Platform able to maintain 300 sustained concurrent streams without queueing >100 ms additional tail latency.

Immediate next steps / action items:
1) I'll share a short MAP and the SLA requirements doc (attached). Please confirm whether the p95/p99 targets above match your internal SLAs.
2) You to share a small set of traces (sample request IDs and any histograms you can easily export) plus a quick note on peak qps and token distribution.
3) Schedule a technical deep-dive with Aditya + Dev next week to go through traces and propose a POC config (batching, KV caching, streaming tuning).

Proposed times for deep-dive: Thu Oct 8 between 9–11am PT or Fri Oct 9 1–3pm PT — which works for your infra team?

Attachments: finly-p95-sla-requirements.pdf (summary of our suggested p95 targets), mutual-action-plan.xlsx (proposed timelines + deliverables).

Thanks — looking forward to narrowing in on the POC plan.

Best,
Marissa

Subject: Re: Discovery Recap: Finly — p95 latency & concurrency requirements

Thanks Marissa — helpful recap and aligned on the goals overall. A few clarifications from our side: 

- The 350 ms p95 for first-byte seems reasonable as a target for short assistant completions; our legal SLA currently only calls out 500 ms p95 for non-streaming calls so this would be an improvement.
- For streaming, the perceived UX break we see is when inter-token gaps exceed ~250 ms consistently, so hitting <=200 ms would be ideal.
- Peak qps: our telemetry shows sustained 280 concurrent streams during heavy business hours, with occasional 800-concurrency bursts during payroll cutover. We'll aim to provide the histograms you requested.

We can do Thu Oct 8 at 10:00am PT for the technical deep-dive — inviting our infra lead Asha. I'll upload the sample traces to the shared Drive link and confirm by end of day.

—Jordan
Jordan Price

Subject: Re: Discovery Recap: Finly — p95 latency & concurrency requirements

Looping in a few quick technical notes ahead of the deep-dive — keeping it high-level so we're not prescriptive until we see traces: 

- Streaming optimizations: we'll look at prefix caching and KV cache hit rates. For your short completions, enabling proactive KV warm-up should reduce cold-LLM latency on first bytes.
- Batching: aim for micro-batches (latency-friendly) instead of large batches; we can use dynamic batching thresholds to maintain <350ms for first-byte while still saving cost.
- Kernel selection & quantization: if you're open to a quantized model variant for non-critical assistant paths, that can reduce per-token time and GPU memory pressure during bursts.
- Fallbacks: propose a graceful degradation policy that switches to a smaller model variant at high concurrency rather than queueing; keeps streaming UX smoother.

Can we get: a) request size distribution (prompt + response token counts), b) example traces showing inter-token timing, c) traffic shape for 24hr window? That will let us size the POC infra.

I'll prep an initial POC config doc and a reference GCP deployment layout for Thu's call.

-Aditya
